en: The Apadāna of the Elder Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya Kiṅkaṇipupphavagga 1 The Apadāna of the Elder Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya: In the past, when the lifespan was twenty thousand years, I was a monk named Sāriputta, dwelling in the forest. At that time, there appeared a Buddha named Padumuttara, endowed with the ten powers, the teacher of devas and humans, who had arrived at the supreme enlightenment. Having paid homage to him, I offered three kiṅkaṇi flowers at his feet. Having made that offering, I uttered this aspiration: "May I, through this root of merit, become a disciple of a Buddha in a future age. For eighty-four thousand aeons I experienced the bliss of heaven; for eighty-four thousand aeons I experienced the bliss of the human world. Having passed away from there, I was reborn in the city of Bandhumatī. There, I became the son of King Bandhumanta. When the Blessed One Kassapa, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, arrived at the city of Bandhumatī, I went to see the Teacher. Having seen the Teacher, I took refuge in the Triple Gem. When the Blessed One Kassapa, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Perfectly Enlightened One, was about to pass away, he addressed the monks: "Monks, this is my last instruction: 'It is through heedfulness that the Noble Ones have attained Nibbāna; it is through heedfulness that those still training strive. Having heard these words of the Teacher, I developed the mind of renunciation and dwelt in the forest. Having developed the mind of renunciation, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. I have lived the holy life under the dispensation of the Buddha Kassapa. Having cast off the body, I have now been reborn in the realm of Tusita. Thus did I perform a deed in the past, and by that deed I am now known as Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya. By means of that very deed, I have attained the state of an Arhat. This is the Apadāna of the Elder Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya. It is completed. May there be well-being. May there be success. May there be peace. May there be prosperity. May there be long life. “I saw the stainless Buddha seated amidst the mountains, shining like a *kaṇikāra* flower.”
To Vipassī, the Leader of the World,
I took three kiṅkaṇī flowers and offered them.
Having worshipped the Fully Enlightened One,
I go facing the south.
By that well-performed deed, [may I attain the fruit of my merit].
And through my volition and aspiration,
having cast off this human body,
I went to the realm of the Tāvatiṃsa gods.
In the ninety-first aeon,
because I worshipped that Buddha,
I have not known a miserable rebirth.
This is the fruit of worshipping the Buddha:
my defilements have been incinerated,
and all states of existence have been utterly eradicated.
Like a snake that has severed its bonds,
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
In the presence of my Buddha,
the three knowledges have been attained;
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges,
these eight liberations,
and the six direct knowledges have been realized.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya recited these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Tikiṅkaṇipupphiya.
